title: School
tagline: Help Meera get her seat in class.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Meera and her Amma have just moved to a new town. Today, Meera wants to join the government school.

nodes.speaker: meera
nodes.text: I'm so excited, Amma! New friends, new books!

nodes.speaker: clerk
nodes.text: Admission? The session started months ago. And where is her birth certificate?

nodes.speaker: amma
nodes.text: We lost it when we moved. We only have her old report card.

nodes.speaker: clerk
nodes.text: No certificate, no admission. Or pay a ₹5,000 'donation' and I'll see what I can do.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Meera looks at Amma. They don't have ₹5,000. What should Meera do?

choices.label: Say "Every child has the right to school" and ask to meet the headteacher.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Meera stays home. Months pass. Other children are learning to read chapter books, and Meera is missing out.

nodes.speaker: mitthu
nodes.text: Hmm, is that fair? School is Meera's right. Let's try again!

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Amma borrows money from a moneylender. Now the family owes a big debt.

nodes.speaker: mitthu
nodes.text: Wait! A school is not allowed to ask for a 'donation' for admission. Try again!

nodes.speaker: meera
nodes.text: Every child has the right to go to school. Can we please meet the headteacher?

nodes.speaker: kaur
nodes.text: You're absolutely right, Meera. A school can't refuse you because of a missing birth certificate, and it can't ask for any donation.

nodes.speaker: kaur
nodes.text: You can join Class 5 today, even in the middle of the year. We'll help your family get a new birth certificate later.

nodes.speaker: narrator
nodes.text: Meera spoke up and got her seat in class. Knowing your rights helps!

card.title: Right to Education
card.kid: Every child aged 6 to 14 can go to a government school for free. A school can't turn you away for a missing birth certificate or ask for a 'donation'. Teachers are not allowed to hit or insult you.
card.teen: The RTE Act, 2009 makes free and compulsory elementary education a right for every child aged 6 to 14. Schools can't charge capitation fees or screen children for admission, can't deny admission for lack of age proof, and must admit a child even after the session has started. Physical punishment and mental harassment are banned. Private unaided schools must reserve 25% of entry-level seats for children from weaker and disadvantaged groups.
card.ifItHappens: Talk to the headteacher or the School Management Committee. You can also call 1098.
card.source: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 (Sections 12, 13, 14, 15, 17); Constitution of India, Article 21A

questions.q: Under the RTE Act, school is free and compulsory for children of which ages?
questions.explain: The RTE Act covers every child aged 6 to 14.

questions.q: A school asks for a 'donation' before giving admission. Is that allowed?
options: Yes, if the school is popular
No, schools can't charge capitation fees
questions.explain: Capitation fees and 'donations' for admission are banned under the RTE Act.

questions.q: Riya doesn't have a birth certificate. Can the school refuse her admission?
options: Only if she is new in town
No, missing age proof can't stop admission
questions.explain: No child can be denied admission for lack of age proof.

questions.q: A teacher hits a student for coming late. Is that allowed?
questions.explain: The RTE Act bans physical punishment and mental harassment of children.

questions.q: The school still refuses admission. Who can Meera's family go to?
options: The headteacher or School Management Committee
questions.explain: The headteacher and School Management Committee must help. You can also call 1098.

questions.q: Private unaided schools must reserve what share of entry-level seats for children from weaker and disadvantaged groups?
questions.explain: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act requires 25% of entry-level seats.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution makes education a fundamental right?
questions.explain: Article 21A was added in 2002 and makes education a fundamental right for ages 6 to 14.
